A.why: Matches the upstream helper, adds an explicit NotSupportedError and GenericRelation support, and ships focused tests including the unsupported-backend path; the GFK branch duplicates the helper's logic instead of reusing it.

B.why: Solid helper with backend check, but it also routes single-valued forward FK and reverse O2O through it, which adds scope, and its tests lack skipUnlessDBFeature so they fail on backends without window functions.

C.why: Very thorough tests, but it builds order_by from query.order_by/Meta.ordering instead of the compiler, rewrites _apply_rel_filters beyond what the issue needs, and calls _next_is_sticky() as a bare statement.

D.why: Upstream-equivalent helper with a clean NotSupportedError and a reasonable cache-path guard in prefetch_one_level, but no tests.

E.why: On backends without window functions it still filters the sliced queryset and hits the original error, it uses low_mark/high_mark truthiness instead of is_sliced, it bypasses filter() via add_q, and it has no tests or docs.

F.why: Empty patch; the issue is not addressed.

G.why: Upstream-style helper with router-aware DB resolution and a careful slice restore on the cached queryset, but no tests and a slightly more involved query.py change than needed.

H.why: Cleanest generalization: one predicate/partition_by helper reused by FK, M2M and GenericRelation with router-aware DB resolution, but no tests.

I.why: It covers GFK and reverse O2O, but it stacks a thin wrapper over a second helper, also changes the _apply_rel_filters manager paths beyond the issue's scope, falls back to DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS instead of the router, and adds no tests.
